correctness.rationale: The four irreducible CTMC state balances uniquely fix the stationary law; its \(2\times2\) occupancy determinant is exactly \(F(d)/[a(2e+d)^2Z^2]\). Strict monotonicity in b yields a unique critical curve. The double-root discriminant \(F=F_d=0\) forces the sole positive tangent \(b_*=2\sqrt{e(a+2e)}-3e\) and \(d_*=2e(b_*+e)/(b_*-e)\), available only for \(a>2e\). Endpoints and asymptotic expansion imply the exact negative-positive-negative interval; rational generator replay, zero-crossings and 2103 assertions independently support algebraic arithmetic but do not substitute for all-parameter proof. No unresolved lemma.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The present mechanism is not a special case of any inspected model with its claimed outcome: to cover it, a prior result would need a common-reset binary occupancy generator with suppressed neighbour-dependent establishment, plus a theorem on the covariance sign as its global reset rate varies. A two-site additive-colonization model has \(b\ge a\) and varying shock correlation fraction rather than this regime; three-site and Gaussian synchrony results likewise do not dominate it.

originality.rationale: Statement-level comparison across accessible previously published ecological models, comparable model statements and available mathematical literature did not reveal a dominating statement. Earlier work treats extinction times, mean occupancy, stochastic growth elasticities, stationary transition estimation, or synchronization under different models. New contribution is exact necessary-and-sufficient double stationary covariance reversal for a two-patch inhibitory-colonization CTMC; standard neighbour-enhanced colonization \(b\ge a\) cannot exhibit the effect. Historical priority remains provisional because several older full papers are inaccessible.
residual_risks: The Johst–Drechsler (2003) full paper was unavailable after an OA/preprint search and authorized institutional access was unavailable; its abstract supports a different extinction-time/simulation objective but does not certify entire-paper noncoverage.

The Wilcox–Cairns–Possingham (2006) full paper was unavailable; its abstract describes a stochastic patch-destruction and recolonization model with quasistationary results, so an uninspected equivalent calculation remains possible.

Boswell thesis chapter 4 covers two-patch global catastrophes in a finite Markov framework; inspected chapter focuses on extinction-time moments without immigration, but other possible equivalents require external verification.
General finite-state reliability models under an alternate terminology might encode a mathematically equivalent quadratic stationary association crossing; searches cannot exclude all such literature.
The output has only self-review, not independent verification.

value.rationale: Shared disturbances are ordinarily expected to synchronize populations; this phase diagram shows an exact negative-positive-negative stationary cross-patch association as catastrophe frequency rises, and proves the necessary restrictions \(a>2e\) and inhibitory \(\(b<a\)/2\). Both restrictions distinguish different establishment mechanisms and delimit when the paradox cannot occur. The exact rational witness and complete global parameter classification provide a clear benchmark for ecological stochastic models, without asserting application to measured habitat dynamics. This is a natural structural classification, not a raw table recomputation, arbitrary numeric slice, or mere algebraic restatement.
